# Working with text data

## Why use Regex?

::: {.incremental}
* It is extremely powerful
* It requires less code than base R
* It works beautifully with `stringr`
:::

## Core Regex Building Blocks

| Concept | Symbol in R | What it matches | Example Match |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Any Character** | `.` | Any single character (except a new line) | `a`, `9`, `%` |
| **Digits** | `\\d` | Any single number | `0`, `7` |
| **Words** | `\\w` | Any letter, number, or underscore | `R`, `x`, `_` |
| **Whitespace** | `\\s` | Spaces, tabs, or new lines | (a space) |

## Building a Regex Pattern

Let's extract the username from the text: **`@rstats_guru`**

<br>

::: {.fragment}
**1.** `@` *(Matches the literal @ symbol)*
:::

::: {.fragment}
**2.** `\\w` *(Matches the first word character, the 'r')*
:::

::: {.fragment}
**3.** `+` *(Expands the match to the rest of the word 'stats_guru')*
:::

<br>

::: {.fragment}
**Final Code:** 
`str_extract(text, "@\\w+")`
:::
